messages.subject: measurement invariance with a single-factor scale and categorical items
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to investigate a measurement invariance across two groups for a single-factor scale with categorical items. However, I got warning when I tested threshold invariance. Could you please tell me if there is anything wrong regarding the syntax?

Here is my syntax:

Configural invariance (this did not give warning)

configural_theta <- "
RPI =~ y9RPI1d +  y9RPI3d + y9RPI4d + y9RPI5d +  y9RPI7d + y9RPI8d + y9RPI9d 
y9RPI1d  | t1 
y9RPI3d | t1 
y9RPI4d  | t1 
 y9RPI5d | t1 
y9RPI7d| t1 
y9RPI8d | t1 
y9RPI9d | t1 
y9RPI1d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI1d 
y9RPI3d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI3d 
y9RPI4d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI4d 
y9RPI5d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI5d 
y9RPI7d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI7d 
y9RPI8d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI8d 
y9RPI9d  ~~ c(1, 1)*y9RPI9d 
RPI  ~~ c(1,1)*RPI 
RPI  ~ c(0, 0)*1
"
m_conf_theta <- lavaan(configural_theta, 
                       data = data, group = "ind_col", 
                       parameterization="theta", estimator="wlsmv",
                       auto.fix.first = FALSE)

summary(m_conf_theta, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

Threshold Invariance (this gave warning)

t_inv_theta <- "
RPI =~ y9RPI1d + y9RPI3d + y9RPI4d + y9RPI5d + y9RPI7d + y9RPI8d + y9RPI9d
y9RPI1d | c(t1_1, t1_1)*t1
y9RPI3d | c(t1_2, t1_2)*t1
y9RPI4d | c(t1_3, t1_3)*t1
y9RPI5d | c(t1_4, t1_4)*t1
y9RPI7d | c(t1_5, t1_5)*t1
y9RPI8d | c(t1_6, t1_6)*t1
y9RPI9d | c(t1_7, t1_7)*t1
y9RPI1d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI1d
y9RPI3d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI3d
y9RPI4d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI4d
y9RPI5d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI5d
y9RPI7d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI7d
y9RPI8d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI8d
y9RPI9d ~~ c(1, NA)*y9RPI9d
y9RPI1d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI3d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI4d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI5d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI7d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI8d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI9d ~ c(0, NA)*1
RPI ~~ c(1,1)*RPI
RPI ~ c(0, 0)*1
"
m_t_inv_theta <- lavaan(t_inv_theta,
data = data, group = "ind_col",
parameterization="theta", estimator="wlsmv",
auto.fix.first = FALSE)

Warning message:
  In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
                      lavaan WARNING:
                      The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
                    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
                    (= 2.826546e-18) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the
                    model is not identified.

### When I delete this part
y9RPI1d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI3d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI4d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI5d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI7d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI8d ~ c(0, NA)*1
y9RPI9d ~ c(0, NA)*1)

I got no warning, but I realized that thresholds were not restricted to be equal when I looked at the output. 

Kind regards,

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance with a single-factor scale and categorical items
parts: it is ok to remove the intercepts if there is one threshold per item? ...
I also then tested threshold & loadings invariance, and threshold, loading, & intercept invariance.

With only 1 threshold per item, there is no way to distinguish differences in thresholds, intercepts, or loadings across groups.  So you have to compare your configural model directly to a model with scalar (threshold, loading, & intercept) invariance.  Strict invariance can then still be tested, if you are interested in that.

Does removing the intercept part prevent comparison among the nested models (i.e., the configural model, threshold invariance model, threshold & loading invariance model, and  threshold, loading, & intercept invariance model)?
No, it just prevents independent identification of different sets of variables.  Thus, you have to simultaneously (not separately) test the assumption of equal thresholds, loadings, & intercepts.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance with a single-factor scale and categorical items
parts: is it not possible to use Chen's cutoff criteria as my items are dichotomous?

Even with normal data (which match Chen's conditions), Chen's (or any) rules of thumb derived do not provide consistent decisions across a variety of data and model characteristics.  Fit indices are not meant to be used as test statistics, although confidence intervals have been proposed to use them as such (despite their muddy interpretation making any null hypothesis dubious).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
